brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Clear typographic hierarchy inside cards: bold titles, muted metadata rows with consistent type/size/date triplet pattern.
Spatial canvas concept is genuinely novel — clusters with faint connecting lines hint at topical proximity instead of grid orthodoxy.
Restrained palette with category color chips (green C, red F) lets content breathe and codes clusters without noise.
dominant_weaknesses: Connection lines are too faint and inconsistent — proximity meaning is asserted but not visually proven, undermining the core thesis.
Card placement looks arbitrary rather than semantically clustered; whitespace feels empty rather than purposeful negative space.
Floating minimap and toolbar feel bolted on; no zoom indicator, no cluster labels, no affordance for how to navigate the canvas.
fix_priorities: Strengthen edges/proximity logic: weighted lines, soft cluster halos, or convex hulls so topic grouping is legible at a glance.
Add cluster headers and a zoom/pan affordance — the canvas needs orientation cues to be usable beyond a single screen.
Tighten card alignment to an invisible spatial grid or force-directed rest state so layout feels intentional, not scattered.
Elevate the minimap with current-viewport framing and make the toolbar echo the canvas language (spatial, not chrome).
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept outpaces visceral polish and behavioral clarity — the idea intrigues but the canvas doesn't yet teach you how to read or move through it.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially solves the brief: it abandons the list/grid as promised, but proximity-as-meaning is asserted through layout vibes rather than rigorously visualized.
